newsitem.title: FRANCE: LYONNAISE SEEN TAKING OVER SUEZ - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: LYONNAISE SEEN TAKING OVER SUEZ - PAPER.

text.p: French water company Lyonnaise des Eaux is set to take over holding group Cie de Suez in a planned merger between the two companies, contrary to market expectations that Suez would take over the former, newspaper Le Monde reported on Tuesday.

"The transaction must be done in this way for legal reasons," the report said, quoting a source close to the deal. "If Lyonnaise were taken over by Suez, it would require renegotiating all the contracts...which are in the company's name," the report quoted the source as saying. That carried significant risk of losses, it added.
The two companies have consistently declined comment on newspaper reports they are preparing a merger.
Some market analysts had taken a view Suez would take over Lyonnaise as Suez has larger financial resources and is the biggest shareholder in the utilities company, with a 16.8 percent holding.

Le Monde reported the merger terms may need to include some sort of special payment to Suez minority shareholders, on top of a share exchange expected to be around one Lyonnaise share for every two Suez shares.
Lyonnaise's arch-rival Cie Generale des Eaux (CGE), which is hostile to the Suez merger, has asked the Lazard investment bank to study ways of blocking the move, the newspaper reported.
Among the studies carried out for CGE "for its own information" was a public offer for Suez, the report said.
CGE has said a Suez acquisition did not come within its strategy.
